newsitem.title: THAILAND: Dark horse Thanong is new Thai finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Dark horse Thanong is new Thai finance minister.

text.p: Low-profile banker Thanong Bidaya, named Thailand's new finance minister on Friday, was a dark horse for the job when the search was on for a suitable person.
Other economic heavyweights were well ahead on Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh's list when he shopped around for replacements to the outgoing Amnuay Viravan, political sources said.
As prime candidates one by one turned down offers for the difficult portfolio, Thanong became the best choice left, they said.

The 50-year-old Thanong, president of Thai Military Bank Plc, is best known as a capable banker who managed to turn a bureaucratic institution into a relatively prosperous bank with international exposure after taking the helm in 1992.
But his selection was seen by analysts as an indication that big names were reluctant to associate themselves with Chavalit's government after political plays brought down the respected Amnuay.
Despite his success, Thanong is seen as less illustrious than his predecessor Amnuay, who had a brilliant 30-year public career as a high-profile civil servant, banker and politician.
"Compared to Amnuay's creamy background, Thanong's looks like skimmed milk," said one economist with a foreign brokerage.
Educated in Japan and the United States, Thanong started at Thai Military Bank as a middle-level manager and worked his way up the corporate ladder in the 1980s.
Later he quit the bank and joined telecommunication giant Shinawatra and was the man behind the landing of major contracts for the company.
Thanong rejoined Thai Military Bank in 1992 as president.
While studying in the United States, he did a brief stint as a research assistant at the World Bank in Washington.

Sources at the bank said Thanong enjoys a good relationship with Prime Minister Chavalit, who has sought his advice on the economy and appointed him to his economic team when he ran for elections last year.

"Thanong is the best we can get under the current constraints. He has had a successful career, is market-driven, conservative and has international exposure. And he is fully supported by the premier," said Poosana Preemanoch, deputy secretary-general to the prime minister.

Market analysts said that despite Thanong's good connections with Chavalit, he could run into the same trouble as the non-elected Amnuay. He would also have to prove that he has a mind of his own, they said.
"Although he has credentials as a banker...his low profile implies that he is going to be very vulnerable to being a pawn in yet another political game," said a foreign analyst.
But others said his humbler background could work in his favour as the politicians may not see him as threat.
"Maybe he has a better chance. While the market may be concerned he may not have the same credentials as Amnuay, that may be the good news," said an executive at a leading US investment bank.
"(Politicians) may not see him as much of threat like Amnuay and let him implement financial policies that are already in place."
